content:
rita: Couple thoughts from today's sync: propose a 'tiered escalation + backpressure shim' to make auto-rollbacks safer. idea is small: add an intermediate 'degradation band' and a token-bucket backpressure layer before any rollback. want to validate API contracts and failure modes.

omar: Explain the token-bucket part?

rita: runtime keeps a per-rollout token bucket that limits how fast we can move traffic away from canary. adjudicator issues an action with a desired delta (e.g., cut 30%); runtime consumes tokens and applies partial moves over time. prevents rapid thrashing and reduces blast radius.

jade: Nice. So rollback becomes a paced operation rather than atomic cutover. How do we seed tokens? fixed refill or adaptive?

rita: Two options: static refill (e.g., 5%/min) for predictable behavior, or adaptive refill tied to recovered headroom (if latency drops, refill faster). default to static, opt-in adaptive.

kevin: What about the escalation bands?

rita: Bands are simple enums: GREEN (ok), AMBER (degrade), RED (rollback), ESCALATE (human). adjudicator maps score -> band. Bands attach policy pointers: e.g., AMBER -> start small-model degrade 10% + reduce concurrency; RED -> initiate paced rollback via token-bucket; ESCALATE -> notify on-call and require manual confirm.

omar: We should also include a short-circuit: if safety-critical errors (SLO breach > x) then immediate cut to baseline (bypass token-bucket). i.e., safety overrides.

jade: Agree. Need well-documented override taxonomy: soft (can be throttled) vs hard (instant).

rita: API sketch: POST /v1/rollouts/{id}/snapshot -> {metrics, tags, model_hash}. Response: {band, recommended_delta, confidence, safety_override:false}. Also events: /v1/rollouts/{id}/events is append-only. runtime polls or subscribes.

kevin: What about split-brain: two adjudicators return conflicting bands?

rita: Use leader lease per-rollout. adjudicator instances elect a leader; leader writes verdict into event log with monotonic version. runtime only honors highest-versioned verdict. if two leaders appear, lease system detects conflict and runtime refuses auto-actions until resolution.

omar: Telemetry: need streaming of partial-apply progress (how many tokens consumed, current canary_rate). Also track "rate-of-change" metric to detect oscillation.

jade: On testing: replay must be able to feed the exact token-bucket state. include token_bucket_state in saved snapshots so sim runs deterministically.

orchestrator-bot: [deploy-bot] tiered-escalation-service v0.1 deployed to staging at 2026-03-18T16:20Z :rocket:

kevin: UX: timeline should show band transitions and token-bucket drain graph. quick controls: "drain now" (admin-only) and "pause auto". any UI action emits signed event and increments audit counter.

rita: Failure modes we listed: 1) adjudicator slow/latent -> runtime acts on stale verdicts; mitigation: include verdict_valid_until and runtime rejects expired verdicts. 2) token-bucket corruption -> store token state in WAL (durable) and recover via checkpoint. 3) region divergence -> tags and per-region buckets.

omar: Also consider cost-sensitivity: an action should include estimated_cost_impact so product/risk policies can prefer degrade vs rollback.

jade: Edge-case: cascading degrade where degraded variant can't handle some features (e.g., tool-calls). require compatibility flags and runtime validation pre-apply. if incompatible, escalate.

kevin: Monitoring: alert on long lived AMBER bands (> x minutes), high frequency band flips, high token consumption rate. Add metric safety.band_duration and safety.token_consumed.

rita: Rollout plan: stage 1: recommend-only (no token ops), stage 2: enable token-bucket pacing in internal routes, stage 3: limited auto-apply for low-risk routes, stage 4: broader rollout with per-tenant opt-outs.

orchestrator-bot: [monitor] tiered-escalation.decision-latency.p95 = 1.4s in staging (2026-03-18T16:50Z) :warning:

omar: Action items: I'll draft an RFC with state machine diagrams + token-bucket proto. jade: can you prototype a sim harness for replayable token state? kevin: I'll sketch UI wireframes and audit event shape.

rita: Thanks all — prefer a quick follow-up Wed 09:30. please leave comments on the RFC draft. :+1:
